title: Economic Loss Assessment of Water Supply–Demand Imbalance in the Yellow River Basin Under Low‐Flow Scenarios
content:
ABSTRACT

Low-flow events trigger water-supply shortages and supply–demand imbalances in water-scarce developed basins; assessing their economic losses informs water-security risk identification and water-resources regulation. This paper establishes an economic loss assessment framework integrating water supply variability, water demand constraints, and sectoral disparities. Combining a risk loss integral model with Monte Carlo simulation, it quantifies water shortage economic impacts across agriculture, industry, domestic and ecological sectors for China's Yellow River Basin. Scenarios covering typical low flow years, prolonged low flow periods, and multi-source regulation are constructed for 2022 (baseline) and 2035 (planned) to analyze spatiotemporal loss patterns and mitigation performance. Economic losses rise with low flow severity and spread toward the middle upper reaches. Basin-wide losses reach 74.66–574.82 × 108 CNY for 2022 and 264.11–730.19 × 108 CNY for 2035 across 75%, 90%, and 95% inflow frequency scenarios. Losses accumulate markedly during sustained low flow episodes, mainly hitting Inner Mongolia, Ningxia, Gansu and Shaanxi. Supplementary water measures mitigate losses; combined schemes outperform single interventions, yet marginal benefits decline with increasing water supply volumes. Losses are co-determined by local water endowment, water use structure, alternative water capacity and regulation policies.
